children: Hello. Three law firms spent 49,670 hours since 2020 representing consumers who sued Google for violating their privacy by collecting data about their online activity after they had opted out of being tracked.
The consumers, a class estimated at nearly 100 million people, won at trial last year, with a jury awarding them $425 million. Google said it plans to appeal.

On Friday, a federal judge approved a $147 million payout to the plaintiffs' lawyers-Boies Schiller Flexner, Susman Godfrey and Morgan & Morgan. The hefty sum is in proportion to the high level of risk the legal teams took on, working on contingency, said Richard Seeborg of the U.S. District Court in San Francisco.

"The lawyers are being handsomely rewarded for their success, even as each of the 98 million class members will walk away with less than $5," Seeborg wrote. That's the nature of class actions, he said. "In our system, there is simply no other way to ensure that a defendant that commits a small tort against a large number of people is held accountable."

Hackers in the Qilin ransomware group on Monday published sensitive data online that they claimed to have stolen from the Justice Department's Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The material appears to be related to specific investigations, including data from phone communications and work associated with the Houston office. The ATF declined to confirm the veracity of the leaked information and said it is investigating. The bureau acknowledged the cyber incident last week. (CNN)
The German capital of Berlin has refused to pay a ransom to hackers who breached the city's network in August. Officials haven't named the group or the sum demanded. (SecurityWeek)

Help for water defense: The Environmental Protection Agency launched a $11.75 million grant program to help 10 water facilities improve their cybersecurity and resiliency after extreme weather events. The facilities, which are in California, Colorado, Florida, Indiana, Kansas and Texas, serve a population of 10,000 or more people.

Separately, the Trump administration kicked off Project Watershed 250, a program to provide free AI and cyber tools and services to water plants across the U.S., starting in Texas. Amazon Web Services, Dragos and Zscaler are among the 13 companies participating. (Axios)

Financial tech provider Jack Henry & Associates said Monday it won't pay a ransom demanded by hacker group ShinyHunters. A voice phishing attack recently got the attackers into the company's internal network and led to the compromise of personal data for "fewer than 10" of its 7,200 clients, according to a disclosure.

Number of cybersecurity regulations across 37 federal agencies that apply to companies and organizations in nine critical infrastructure sectors, according to a study by the Government Accountability Office.

CISO move: David Soto joined cybersecurity provider Trellix as CISO after leading infrastructure security at Amazon.com for more than four years. Soto has also held senior security positions at Check Point Software Technologies, Optiv and Pacific Life Insurance.
